newsitem.title: UK: Shell gains ahead of presentation.
newsitem.headline: Shell gains ahead of presentation.

text.p: Shares in Shell Transport and Trading Co Plc rose 10-1/2p to 983-1/2 after a newspaper report on planned downstream investments raised hopes of favourable statements during upcoming presentations to analysts.

Royal Dutch/Shell Group will meet analysts in New York on Friday and in London on Monday. The Financial Times reported on Thursday that the Anglo-Dutch oil giant planned to spend up to $10 billion in oil production projects in the Gulf of Mexico.
"It raises expectations for the presentations," an analyst said. Royal Dutch/Shell Group declined to comment on the FT report, referring queries to its U.S. unit Shell Oil.
The FT said Shell Oil would spend $10 billion over the next four years in deep-water oil production with eight projects in preparation.
Analysts said they would welcome such an investment. "It is good news. They are investing where the money is," said analyst Jurjen Lunshof at Credit Lyonnais Laing.
Low development costs and a readily available infrastructure mean that the Gulf of Mexico is a profitable upstream area for Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said John Toalster at SocGen.
"It is very profitable oil," he said.
